page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The CPU architecture incorporates Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512, and cryptographic hardware flags. The system features 192 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a standard 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 9 Gbps. This configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators or attached local NVMe storage.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem bandwidth, reaching 222.41 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 94.88 GB/sec on writes. High-throughput execution is demonstrated by 64.03 million Redis SET operations per second, 73.67 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and strong software compilation scores in Geekbench (45,645). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 309.94 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks show moderate baseline CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core results placing in the middle 50% category.

Because the server uses a burstable CPU allocation model, m7i-flex.12xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with fluctuating demand compared to fixed-performance instances. Continuous full-core load may incur CPU credit constraints over time. Given its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM memory balance and high memory throughput, this server is suitable for application backends, web serving, database tasks, software build pipelines, and medium-parameter model prompt processing.
